extracted.intended_audience: regulatory stakeholders, attorneys, industry and members of the public monitoring Department of Justice rulemaking and Federal Register notices
extracted.subtask_description: An API/listing of Department of Justice (DOJ) Federal Register documents (notices, proposed rules, and final rules) describing regulatory actions and procedural notices that may be subject to notice-and-comment. Useful for parties tracking rulemaking, information-collection requests, consent decrees, and statutory-conforming regulatory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) — OMB review and approval of information collection requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection requests must be submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to DOJ components (e.g., ATF, Office of Juvenile Justice) when proposing or revising forms or data collections (e.g., Form 4473, generic clearances for studies). The listing identifies that DOJ will submit such requests to OMB and solicit public comment in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Youth Handgun Safety Act — FFL posting and written notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under existing Department regulations implementing the Youth Handgun Safety Act, federal firearms licensees (FFLs) who deliver handguns to non-licensees must post signs and provide written notice regarding the Act's provisions to each handgun purchaser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ATF's proposed rule would remove this regulatory requirement; the description frames the posting and written-notice obligation as a current compliance duty for FFLs that could be rescinded if the rule is finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import eligibility for dual-use frames, receivers, or barrels — sporting-configuration requirement at time of import
rubrics_metrics.description: Dual-use frames, receivers, or barrels may be lawfully imported if, at the time imported, there is an identified firearm sporting configuration for the frame, receiver, or barrel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once in the U.S., the dual-use part may be used to assemble sporting, non-sporting, or NFA firearms provided assembly complies with other federal firearms laws. The criterion centers on the configuration identified at importation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-over-the-counter (NOTC) transfers — background checks, remote identity proofing, and CLEO notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes would permit FFLs to conduct non-over-the-counter sales (transfers to persons who do not appear in person) while complying with background check requirements and would add remote identity proofing and electronic notices to chief law enforcement officers (CLEOs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule would remove limits that restricted NOTC transfers to background-check-exempt transfers and would add procedures (remote identity proofing, electronic CLEO notice) intended to preserve background-check protections while allowing remote transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: NFA interstate transport and temporary export — duration-based notification/approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ATF proposes to no longer require persons transporting certain NFA firearms within the U.S. for short-term purposes (365 days or fewer) to submit notice to ATF and await approval; persons transporting for long-term (>365 days) or permanent relocation would no longer have to await approval after submitting notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion divides transport/temporary export rules by duration (short-term vs long-term/permanent) and adjusts the prior notice-and-wait-for-approval process accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import exclusion for items in foreign-trade zones (FTZs) and customs-bonded warehouses (CBWs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendment to exclude from the Gun Control Act (GCA) and National Firearms Act (NFA) import requirements items brought into customs-bonded warehouses (in addition to FTZs) and to remove the condition that items may be brought in only 'for storage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed exclusion would not exempt merchandise from customs requirements. The criterion concerns when import requirements are triggered based on location and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory conformity with statutory changes (e.g., NFA tax remittance rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations must be amended as necessary to reflect statutory changes to ensure ATF regulations are current and consistent with the statute (example: conforming NFA tax remittance provisions to changes made by statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When statutes change (e.g., via legislation like the referenced OBBBA), agencies must update implementing regulations to conform; the document frames this as a necessary regulatory housekeeping/consistency requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraband Cigarette Trafficking Act implementation — jurisdictional thresholds, covered products, and record/reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing amendments include reducing the quantity threshold that triggers CCTA jurisdiction (from >60,000 to >10,000), extending coverage to contraband smokeless tobacco, expanding record-keeping requirements, and imposing reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bundle of criteria governs when the statute applies (threshold quantities), the scope of covered products, and the documentary/reporting duties imposed on regulated parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of temporary imports to permanent imports for defense articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed provision allowing importers to apply for ATF authorization to convert items temporarily imported (under DOS authorization or EAR temporary-import provisions) into permanent imports in compliance with other federal firearms laws, without exporting and reimporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criterion sets forth an administrative authorization pathway for conversion, subject to compliance with other applicable firearms and export/import laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions related to mental-health disqualifiers for firearms possession
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments to update the definitions of 'adjudicated as a mental defective' and 'committed to a mental institution' in ATF regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to these definitions affect eligibility/disqualification for firearms transactions and possession; the criterion is the statutory/regulatory definitional standard that triggers disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'willfully' for firearms violations
rubrics_metrics.description: ATF proposes a regulatory definition of the term 'willfully' in regulations implementing the Gun Control Act, specifying the mental state required for certain firearm-related offenses under Department regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying mens rea in regulation affects enforcement scope and culpability; the proposal aims to define 'willfully' consistently with statutory and interpretive considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and standards for firearms electronic record-keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule to authorize federal firearms licensees (FFLs) to generate, maintain, and store records in an electronic record-keeping system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion governs whether and how regulated parties may use electronic systems in place of paper records; implementation details (security, retention, accessibility) would be addressed in the full rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint NFA registration for spouses
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed regulatory change to authorize spouses to file a joint application to make, transfer or receive, and register a firearm under the NFA; if approved, both spouses would have joint rights and transfers between them would not constitute a further transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alters registration and transfer mechanics under the NFA, removing the need for an additional transfer application when moving an NFA firearm between jointly-registered spouses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions to Firearms Transaction Record (Form 4473) — identity verification, timeframes, and electronic features
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed regulatory amendments to Form 4473 and related rules that would: streamline identity and residence verification requirements and documents; double the performance timeframe for transactions following a NICS check; permit electronic forms and notices, auto-population, and attached copies; address private-party transfers and firearms handler checks; incorporate ATF rulings and other guidance; align regulations with statutory text; and make technical revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a multi-part criterion affecting transaction processing (timelines), acceptable identity/residence documentation, electronic form functionality (auto-fill, attachments), treatment of private transfers, and harmonization of regulations with statutory language and existing ATF guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsiveness to public comments — publishing responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The listing includes a 'Response to Public Comments' document (e.g., in litigation or settlement contexts), showing a practice of publishing agency responses to public comments as part of the administrative record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agencies receive public comments on rulemakings or settlements, they may publish collated responses; this supports transparency and the administrative record used in final decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of lodging of proposed consent decrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of lodging of proposed consent decrees (under statutes like the Clean Water Act or Clean Air Act) are published in the Federal Register to provide public notice of pending settlements between DOJ and settling parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural requirement ensures public awareness and opportunity to review proposed settlements; the Federal Register notice is the mechanism for lodging/public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity of regulatory definitions with judicial decisions (example: machine-gun definition post-Supreme Court)
rubrics_metrics.description: ATF is amending regulatory definitions (e.g., 'machine gun') in response to Supreme Court decisions (example: removing sentences that incorporated bump stocks into machine-gun definitions after the Court held ATF exceeded statutory authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations must be revised where courts interpret statutory scope and agency action exceeded authority; this criterion requires agencies to align regulatory language with controlling judicial rulings.
